SQL:
SELECT
  DATE_TRUNC('DAY', orders.order_date) AS "orders.order_date",
  CAST(SUM(orders.amount) AS DOUBLE) AS "orders.rev"
FROM orders AS orders
WHERE
  (
    orders.order_date >= CAST('2025-01-01' AS DATE)
    AND orders.order_date < CAST('2026-01-01' AS DATE)
  )
GROUP BY
  DATE_TRUNC('DAY', orders.order_date)
LIMIT 21

SQL:
WITH _base AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(ISODOW(orders.order_date) AS INT) AS "orders.dow",
    CAST(SUM(orders.amount) AS DOUBLE) AS "orders.rev"
  FROM orders AS orders
  WHERE
    orders.order_date >= CAST('2025-01-01' AS DATE)
    AND orders.order_date < CAST('2026-01-01' AS DATE)
  GROUP BY
    CAST(ISODOW(orders.order_date) AS INT)
), _cm_orders__amount_sum_partition_by AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(SUM(orders.amount) AS DOUBLE) AS "orders.amount_sum_partition_by"
  FROM orders AS orders
  WHERE
    orders.order_date >= CAST('2025-01-01' AS DATE)
    AND orders.order_date < CAST('2026-01-01' AS DATE)
)
SELECT
  _base."orders.dow",
  _base."orders.rev",
  _base."orders.rev" / _cm_orders__amount_sum_partition_by."orders.amount_sum_partition_by" AS "orders.share"
FROM _base
CROSS JOIN _cm_orders__amount_sum_partition_by
ORDER BY
  _base."orders.dow" ASC
LIMIT 21

args.message: In 2025, Sunday (day 7) brought in the most revenue, at 18,176.28 or about 15.8% of the year. Monday (day 1) was close behind at 17,801.52 (about 15.5%). Thursday (day 4) was the lowest at 14,658.31 (about 12.7%). Revenue is the sum of order amounts for all orders dated in 2025, with no filter on order status. Days are numbered the ISO way, Monday = 1 through Sunday = 7. Each share is that day's revenue divided by the 2025 total, and the seven shares add up to 1.
